scope: Definite named-person or ruler omissions only (not stylistic compression). Remaining 130+ map units are editorial style holds, not certified omissions.

replacements.current: Sima Wei's coup caught the new throne blind.
replacements.replacement: When the emperor had just taken the throne, Prince Chu Wei forged edicts to execute Prince Runan Liang and Grand Tutor Wei Guan, and the emperor could not see through it.
replacements.reason: 汝南王亮、太保衛瓘 must appear; 楚王瑋 is Prince Chu Wei, not a generic "coup."

replacements.current: The tree marked the whirl of four emperors.
replacements.replacement: When Xiaowu was only four, Ai soon died, Haixi took the throne and was soon deposed, Jianwen crossed from a prince's fief to inherit the great enterprise and ruled less than two years, then Xiaowu succeeded.
replacements.reason: 孝武、哀帝、海西、簡文 succession chain is explicit in 時孝武年始四歲…而孝武嗣統.

replacements.current: Twin black birds presaged Ming-di's death.
replacements.replacement: In Emperor Ming's eighth month, on gengxu, two great bluish-black birds with wings one zhang four chi wide appeared; one perched at the Minister of Education's residence and was shot dead, the other at a north-city household and was also taken.
replacements.reason: 明帝、司徒府、庚戌 omen facts are dropped; death is not stated in the unit.

replacements.replacement: Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Prince of Eastern Ying Teng Sima Teng moved his command from Bingzhou to garrison Ye, passing Zhengding en route.
replacements.reason: 東嬴王騰 and the march to 鄴 are explicit; Sima Teng alone omits title and route.
